messages:
kyle: heads-up — customer TKT-4567 reporting big throughput drop on their Dedicated pool (eu-west). Started ~23:05 UTC. latency went from ~60ms to 240-800ms, and they see intermittent 429s.

anita: looking at metrics now. queued_requests spiked, but GPU utilization stayed mid 60s. suspicious: avg batch tokens down to ~24. suspect micro-batching. :thinking:

sasha: autoscaler didn't kick. pool utilization ~72% for ~12m, but scale_up_threshold is 85% and cooldown is 5m so it stayed put. config might be too conservative for bursts.

maria: support says no billing/auth errors in the ticket. support-bot confirms no quota changes. customer has reserved capacity, so billing gating unlikely.

kyle: paste of the snapshot metrics I pulled: `queued_requests=312`, `in_flight=30`, `avg_batch_size_tokens=24`, `median_batch_count=3`, `gpu_util=0.62`, `throttle_429=16/min`

anita: here's the runtime scheduler excerpt from the node handling that pool (sanitized):
```
scheduler:
  continuous_batching: true
  max_batch_tokens: 32
  batch_window_ms: 10
  prefer_token_packing: false

autoscaler:
  scale_up_threshold: 0.85
  cooldown_s: 300
  min_instances: 2
```

anita: note `max_batch_tokens: 32` + very small `batch_window_ms` -> lots of small batches. continuous batching with tiny window often creates many tiny micro-batches, hurting throughput.

sasha: also saw heavy tail of large-context requests from tenant `nlp-research` during the window. Those requests lock the KV cache and prefill threads, blocking efficient packing for other tenants (noisy neighbor).

tom: reproducer steps I used in staging:
1) spin up 4 clients hitting the dedicated pool with mixed context sizes (40/1024 tokens) at ~220 rps total
2) observe batch sizes in runtime dashboard
3) toggle `prefer_token_packing` and bump `batch_window_ms` -> batch sizes increase, latency drops

anita: quick test command I ran: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer xxx" -d @mix-requests.json https://dedicated.redwood.internal/v1/generate` — when I set `max_batch_tokens=512` and `batch_window_ms=40`, avg batch tokens jumped to ~420 and throughput recovered ~+35%. no scale events triggered though.

maria: so root causes: (1) scheduler params favor micro-batches (max_batch_tokens too low + tiny window) (2) autoscaler thresholds too conservative for bursty mix (3) noisy tenant creating head-of-line KV prefill blocking.

sasha: mitigation plan:
- short term (canary NOW): increase `max_batch_tokens` to 512 and `batch_window_ms` to 40ms on one pool shard (staging -> canary in prod shard A). enable `prefer_token_packing=true`. monitor 15m.
- medium: reduce autoscaler cooldown to 90s and lower scale_up_threshold to 70% for Dedicated pools with mixed traffic patterns.
- long term: implement per-tenant fair-queueing + prefill isolation and move heavy long-context jobs to separate routing class.

kyle: assigned: anita to run the canary and post graphs, tom to prepare rollback if errors, sasha to draft autoscale change PR, maria to update support ticket with repro and interim workaround (increase batch_window_ms).

anita: starting canary on shard eu-west-2 (pool:d-42-canary) — toggling config now. will post CPU/GPU/batch charts in ~8m. :eyes:

ops-bot: deploy started by anita on pool:d-42-canary at 23:28:11 UTC — config patch id caf3a9

support-bot: updated TKT-4567 — told customer were running a canary and recommended a short-term retry/backoff pattern in their client (exponential backoff up to 200ms).

anita: canary results (8m window): queued_requests down 60%, avg_batch_tokens -> 398, p95 latency from 820ms -> 210ms, no new 5xx/502s, 429s dropped to ~2/min.

sasha: looks good. tom: once PR for autoscaler lands and we monitor one day, we should flip default on other pools. Also schedule a follow-up to evaluate per-tenant isolation.

kyle: great. if any regression, escalate to Incident channel. thanks everyone. :tada:
